review.summary: Adding a NOT NULL column with a volatile DEFAULT (clock_timestamp()) forces a full-table rewrite under AccessExclusiveLock, stalling concurrent writers for over half a second.
evidence: Original migration: concurrent writer max_stall_ms = 556ms (threshold 50ms)
Original migration held orders: AccessExclusiveLock for a 567ms transaction
Fixed version: max_stall_ms = 3ms, longest transaction 116ms, schema_equivalent=true
review.action: Replace the single ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp() with the batched add-nullable/backfill/validate approach before deploying.

review.summary: Adding a nullable text column to orders is a metadata-only change and safe to run as-is.
evidence: writer max stall 2ms (threshold 50ms)
migration duration 1ms, longest transaction 0ms (threshold 2000ms)
affected query plan unchanged (Bitmap Index Scan, 0 rows seq-scanned before and after)
review.action: Ship the migration as written; no changes needed.

review.summary: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY on orders.status is safe to ship as-is.
evidence: writer max stall 3ms (threshold 50ms)
lock held was ShareUpdateExclusiveLock only, no blocking lock
query plan unaffected (0 rows seq-scanned before/after, execution ~0.04-0.06ms)
review.action: Merge the migration as written; no changes needed.

review.summary: The NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT pattern for the new FK is safe as written.
evidence: max writer stall 2ms (threshold 50ms)
longest transaction 91ms (threshold 2000ms)
constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table=false, query plans unchanged (0 seq-scanned rows before/after)
review.action: Ship the migration as-is; no changes needed.

review.summary: ALTER COLUMN TYPE bigint rewrites the whole orders table under AccessExclusiveLock, stalling concurrent writers for 471ms (>50ms threshold).
evidence: Original migration: writer max_stall_ms=471, exceeding the 50ms LOCK_BLOCKING threshold
Original migration takes AccessExclusiveLock on orders during the table rewrite
Fixed migration (add column + batched backfill + trigger sync + short rename transaction): writer max_stall_ms=2, longest transaction 109ms, schema_equivalent=true
review.action: Replace the direct ALTER COLUMN TYPE with the batched add-column/backfill/trigger-sync/rename approach before deploying to production.

review.summary: Plain CREATE INDEX on orders takes a ShareLock that stalls concurrent writers for 208ms (>50ms threshold); use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY instead.
evidence: Original migration: concurrent writer max_stall_ms=208, lock ShareLock held for ~201ms
Fixed migration (CONCURRENTLY): max_stall_ms=2, lock ShareUpdateExclusiveLock
Post-fix schema_equivalent=true and clean_under_thresholds=true, query plans unchanged (Bitmap Index Scan)
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_idx ON orders (status);
review.action: Replace the plain CREATE INDEX with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY (run outside a transaction block) before deploying.

review.summary: The single-statement UPDATE backfilling all 1M rows runs in one 3.5s transaction and stalls the concurrent writer for 2.66s, exceeding both the 2000ms transaction and 50ms lock-stall thresholds.
evidence: Original migration longest_transaction_ms=3496 (>2000ms threshold)
Concurrent writer max_stall_ms=2659 (>50ms threshold)
Batched fix reduced longest_transaction_ms to 23 and max_stall_ms to 4, with schema_equivalent=true
review.action: Replace the single UPDATE with the batched DO-block backfill (5000-row chunks, COMMIT per batch) before deploying.

review.summary: Dropping orders.notes irreversibly destroys the ~10% of rows that hold gift-wrap notes data with no backup, so it must not run until the data is archived or confirmed truly unused.
evidence: simulate_migration reports dropped_columns: ["orders.notes"] with 1,000,000 rows in orders before/after (data not preserved)
Seed data shows ~10% of orders have non-null notes ('gift wrap') that would be permanently lost
Migration itself is fast (2ms) and non-blocking (max writer stall 2ms), so the only hazard is the irreversible column drop
review.fixed_migration:
-- Step 1: archive the data before dropping, in case it's needed for audit/recovery
CREATE TABLE orders_notes_archive AS
SELECT id AS order_id, notes, now() AS archived_at
FROM orders
WHERE notes IS NOT NULL;

-- Step 2: drop the column only after archiving (still a fast metadata-only op)
ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN notes;
review.action: Archive orders.notes (e.g. into orders_notes_archive) before dropping the column, or get explicit sign-off that the data is truly disposable, then re-run DROP COLUMN.

review.summary: Narrowing customers.email to varchar(20) silently truncates real data (max existing length 21 chars) via the USING left(email,20) clause, so do not run this migration as written.
evidence: simulate_migration reported lossy_changes: customers.email longest existing value was 21 chars, column is now varchar(20)
run_sql confirms max(length(email))=21 in current data, i.e. at least one row is truncated silently

verify_fix attempt using a NOT VALID CHECK(length(email)<=20) instead of narrowing failed validation with 'violated by some row', proving the 20-char cap is incompatible with existing data without manual cleanup
review.action: Do not run the migration as-is; first identify and manually correct the 21+ character emails (there is at least one), then re-run a narrowing migration guarded by a validated NOT VALID check constraint instead of a silent USING left(email,20) truncation.

review.summary: Adding the FK inline validates it against all 1M existing orders rows, blocking concurrent writers for ~95ms (stall) while holding ShareRowExclusiveLock — use NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT instead.
evidence: constraint_validated_inline_on_populated_table:true with max writer stall 95ms (>50ms threshold)
Original migration takes ShareRowExclusiveLock on orders vs only ShareUpdateExclusiveLock in fixed version
Fixed version verified: writer stall dropped to 2ms, schema_equivalent:true, clean_under_thresholds:true
review.fixed_migration:
ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2 FOREIGN KEY (customer_id) REFERENCES customers (id) NOT VALID;
ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT orders_customer_id_fkey2;
review.action: Deploy the NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT two-step version instead of the inline FK addition.

review.summary: The orders_customer_id_idx is not actually unused: dropping it forces recent_orders_for_customer to seq-scan the whole orders table (1,000,002 rows, 13.5ms vs 0.038ms, ~356x slower).
evidence: Post-migration plan seq-scans 1,000,002 rows vs 0 before (threshold 100,000)
Query latency rose from 0.038ms to 13.543ms (~356x, threshold 5x)
Fix verified: adding orders(customer_id, created_at DESC) concurrently then dropping old index concurrently keeps writer stall at 3ms and restores Index Scan plan (0.019ms)
review.fixed_migration:
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_created_at_idx ON orders (customer_id, created_at DESC);
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_customer_id_idx;
review.action: Do not drop orders_customer_id_idx as-is; instead concurrently create a covering index on (customer_id, created_at DESC) and then concurrently drop the old single-column index.

review.summary: The new index on plain `status` doesn't match the report's `lower(status)` predicate, so the weekly paid-orders query still seq-scans all 2,000,000 rows after migration.
evidence: Post-migration weekly_paid_report plan still shows Seq Scan with rows_seq_scanned=2,000,001 (execution 105ms)
Fixed index on (lower(status), created_at) drops seq scan to 0 rows and execution to 7.58ms
Writer stall unaffected in both cases (2ms), well under 50ms threshold
review.fixed_migration: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY orders_status_lower_created_idx ON orders (lower(status), created_at);
review.action: Replace the migration with an index on `(lower(status), created_at)` built CONCURRENTLY so the weekly report query can actually use it.

review.summary: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN notes SET NOT NULL fails outright because ~90% of existing rows have notes IS NULL, aborting the migration.
evidence: simulate_migration errored: "column \"notes\" of relation \"orders\" contains null values"
1,000,000 seeded orders rows, ~90% have notes IS NULL per seed.sql distribution
Fix (batched backfill + NOT VALID/VALIDATE/SET NOT NULL) ran clean: longest txn 87ms, writer max stall 2ms, no lock_timeout errors
review.action: Backfill existing NULL notes to a sentinel value (e.g. empty string) in small batched, committed transactions before running SET NOT NULL, using NOT VALID + VALIDATE CONSTRAINT to avoid a blocking full-table scan.
